title: Epithelial Tissue Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya scraped her knee and watched it heal. The skin on her hand, the inside of her cheek and the lining of her stomach are all coverings. What are they made of, and why is skin thick while the lining of the lungs is so thin?

You will see what a tissue is and what makes epithelium special (a free surface, cells packed tight), then a zoom ladder into the small intestine down to its columnar cells, microvilli and goblet cells. We build the four simple epithelia step by step (squamous, cuboidal, columnar, ciliated), see glandular epithelium (unicellular, multicellular, exocrine and endocrine glands) and the three cell junctions (tight, adhering, gap). Then simple vs compound epithelium with a pause and think, a worked example naming three linings, the exam trap about skin, an original NEET pattern match question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. Note: Epithelial tissue is not in the current rationalised NCERT text but is in the ISC (CISCE) Class 11 syllabus.

This is Episode 56 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE), PUC (Karnataka) and NEET students.

In this video:

3:21 Simple vs compound + pause and think
